answer: A key must lock 140 POA against one registered electricity service point. Mid-epoch the ISO writes a 16-byte nonce into that meter's ANSI C12.22 association; the C12 key on file has nine seconds to sign H(epoch-seed || meter-serial || nonce). A second wallet on the same serial or service-point is merged and loses 70 POA, so names behind one building feed still count as one principal. I verified the frame at a karst-side substation and posted it, in a velvet sleeve, to the public forge of bound meters. Traces stay public four epochs; leftover collateral refunds after three sealed answers.
